clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 0-754 of the held text jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8554-exemption-william-t-andrews-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt): signed September 28, 1940. The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be further exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), further exempts William T. Andrews from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. The recital names the earlier exemption Executive Order No. 8228 of August 24, 1939; those are earlier instruments, not events on this order. First end: the order's own stated end, September 30, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of September 30, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when September 30, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held. MOMMSEN-I rechecked this stated end against both held witnesses.
